prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Aliases: Medication Order Gateway=Morrowglass; Pharmacy Technician=Copperfield; Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot=Cinderwake; Pharmacy Verification Station=Juniper; Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler=Bluejay; Registered Nurse=Larkspur; Medication Return Kiosk=Tallowmere; Biomedical Engineer=Stonewake. Morrowglass validates patient/product/dose/route/timing, timestamps orders, retains rejection reasons, produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. Cinderwake uses snapshot for stable-identifier order/dispense/cabinet reconciliation, preserving context/details/authorization/timestamps/transaction-identifiers; records matches/differences/disposition. Cancellations excluded; corrections authoritative; superseded values discarded; duplicates reviewed; partial-dispense remainder conservative. Disagreements/unresolved transactions held; Copperfield authorizes routine replenishment only with clear reconciliation queue. Clinical Pharmacist assesses clinical exceptions, produces Dose Exception Review Slip; documented authorized disposition precedes release; corrections require valid orders, not history inference. Inconclusive review stays held pending higher clinical decision. Final disposition records reviewer/evidence/release/correction/withholding; observers immediately escalate serious/time-critical exceptions. Medication Safety Officer reviews suspected diversion/repeated high-risk exceptions/potential patient harm. IT Operations Specialist receives Diversion Review Packet, examines access/transaction/device logs without altering clinical disposition, records software/connectivity findings. Stonewake assesses mechanical/sensor faults and safe return-to-service. Cinderwake stops affected picks, retains scanned product/quantity, controls holds, produces Priority Refill Tote Tag, presents packages to Juniper. Juniper verifies order/product/strength/measured-quantity, blocks incomplete/mismatched verification, records evidence/disposition/reviewer, produces Batch Release Note. Copperfield checks contents/identifiers/packaging/lot/expiry/cold-chain, produces Cold Chain Handoff Card. Bluejay logs temperatures/reports excursions/connectivity-loss; affected stock segregated pending assessment. Hospital Courier records custody, produces Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record; Pneumatic Tube Network reconciles loads/destinations; manifest records packages/destinations/handling/assembly-time. East Tube Dispatch Console reports availability/routes/status, sends Tube Route Exception Ticket; West Tube Dispatch Console controls authorized routing. Discrepancies hold loads; retries require rechecks; faults testing/authorization; unavailable automation approved alternate delivery/custody. Ward staff verify receipts; Larkspur checks refrigeration/locks transactions. North Ward Cabinet Controller uses tote tag/blocks holds; South Ward Cabinet Controller reports lock/access failures; both record arrivals/destinations.

New part:
S161: North Ward Cabinet Controller applies the North Ward medication access rules when evaluating a cabinet transaction.
S162: Its ward-specific configuration defines permitted medication locations, access roles, and transaction limits for each cabinet.
S163: The configuration associates each medication location with the product identifiers and quantity thresholds used by the ward.
S164: Cabinet availability is calculated from the last confirmed inventory count and subsequent recorded movements.
S165: Configured maximum and minimum quantities guide replenishment decisions without overriding an active clinical restriction.
S166: Access rules require an authenticated user role appropriate to the requested medication and transaction type.
S167: High-risk medication locations can require an additional confirmation before a removal is accepted.
S168: The controller rejects a transaction when its location mapping does not match the reconciled medication identity.
S169: Configuration changes are versioned, reviewed, and recorded with the effective time and approving authority.
S170: If the controller has not received a current approved configuration, it prevents routine dispensing and reports the condition for investigation.
S171: Bluejay maintains a time-stamped temperature history for each refrigerated medication compartment and raises an alarm when a configured limit is exceeded.
S172: Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler applies approved upper and lower temperature limits to each monitored compartment.
S173: Calibrated probes report readings at configured intervals, and the cooler records probe identity and calibration status with each reading.
S174: Refrigerated stock is identified by medication, lot, and expiration date so that each unit remains traceable to its storage history.
S175: When readings exceed a limit or a probe becomes unavailable, the affected stock is marked ineligible for routine dispensing.
S176: The cooler preserves the affected stock in its current controlled environment while the condition is assessed.
S177: Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler uses the handoff card to compare a transfer’s recorded custody time with its temperature history.
S178: A Clinical Pharmacist reviews excursion details and determines whether affected stock may be released, quarantined, or discarded under pharmacy policy.
S179: The cooler retains the disposition status against the affected lot and prevents stock marked ineligible from being selected for routine dispensing.
S180: Authorized access to refrigerated compartments is recorded with the user identity, access time, and affected stock identifiers.
S181: Door-open duration is monitored so that an access event that threatens temperature control can be distinguished from a brief inspection.
S182: Temperature alarms remain active during loss of network connectivity, and local records are retained until communication is restored.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
